title: Substantiation for superlative and No.1 claims
text: Under FTC guidance, superlative or '#1' claims must be supported by competent and reliable evidence, such as a cited third-party survey, that exists at the time the claim is made.

title: Substantiation for quantified performance
text: Specific performance or savings figures (e.g., 'saves 50% on energy') require competent and reliable scientific evidence, and the material test conditions must be disclosed.

title: Former price for discount claims
text: A discount or 'was/now' claim must reference a bona fide former price at which the product was openly offered for a reasonably substantial period of time.

title: Disclosure of 'free' offer terms
text: When advertising an item as 'free', all terms, conditions, and obligations upon which receipt of the free item is contingent must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously at the outset.

title: Qualification of general environmental claims
text: Under the FTC Green Guides, unqualified general environmental benefit claims such as 'eco-friendly' or 'green' are deceptive unless qualified with the specific, substantiated benefit they refer to.

title: Honest and typical testimonials
text: Endorsements must reflect the honest opinions of the endorser and depict typical results; if results are atypical, a clear and conspicuous disclaimer of the generally expected results is required.

title: Substantiation for health and germ-kill claims
text: Health, safety, or efficacy claims (e.g., 'kills 99.9% of germs') require competent and reliable scientific evidence, including the tested organisms and conditions.
